sections.title: The Concept: From ODEs to PDEs (60s)
sections.content: Transition from Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) which involve one independent variable, to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) which involve multiple independent variables (time and space). Use a visual transition of a single point moving on a line (ODE) vs. a vibrating string or a heat map (PDE).
sections.example: Compare a 'single bee' flying in a line (ODE) to a 'swarm of bees' spreading across a 2D meadow (PDE).

sections.title: Core Mechanism: Partial Derivatives (90s)
sections.content: Explain the concept of partial derivatives as 'rate of change in one direction while holding others constant.' Use 3D surface plots where slice lines represent the partial derivative with respect to X or T.
sections.example: A hiker on a mountain: The slope along the 'East-West' path (∂f/∂x) vs. the slope along the 'North-South' path (∂f/∂y).

sections.title: The Heat Equation: A Classic Example (90s)
sections.content: Introduce the Heat Equation: ∂u/∂t = α∇²u. Explain that the rate of temperature change at a point is proportional to the local curvature (laplacian) of the temperature distribution. Visualize a metallic rod cooling down via a color-coded gradient animation.
sections.example: A smartphone battery overheating: Seeing the heat spread from the CPU chip across the phone casing over time.

sections.title: Boundary & Initial Conditions (60s)
sections.content: Explain that PDEs require 'Initial Conditions' (what happens at T=0) and 'Boundary Conditions' (constraints at the edges) to have a unique solution. Visualize a drum head being hit (Initial) and held tight by a frame (Boundary).
sections.example: A guitar string: The initial pluck (Initial) and the anchored ends at the bridge and tuning peg (Boundary).

storyboard.title: The Concept: From ODEs to PDEs (60s)
lecture_lines: ODEs relate one variable, like a moving point.
PDEs involve multiple variables, like time and space.
Think of a single bee versus a swarm.
animations: Display title '#000000' background with 'ODE vs PDE' text in #FFFFFF color.
Show a single variable function graph in #FF0000 representing an ODE.
Transition to a multi-variable surface plot in #00FF00 representing a PDE.
Highlight the transition from total to partial derivatives using #FFFF00.
Fade out all elements to transition to next section.

storyboard.title: Core Mechanism: Partial Derivatives (90s)
lecture_lines: Partial derivatives measure rates in specific directions.
Imagine a hiker traversing a mountain surface.
Slope changes differently along East-West versus North-South paths.
We hold one coordinate constant while varying another.
This reveals the rate of change in that direction.
animations: Animate a plane slice along $x$ to show $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ in #00FF00.
Animate a plane slice along $y$ to show $\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ in #0000FF.
Summarize both derivatives with text in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: The Heat Equation: A Classic Example (90s)
lecture_lines: The Heat Equation describes how temperatures evolve.
Rate of temperature change relates to local curvature.
Heat spreads naturally to balance temperature differences.
Curvature, or the Laplacian, drives this diffusion.
Visualize heat diffusing across a metallic rod.
animations: Display title 'The Heat Equation' in #FFFFFF color.
Overlay the heat equation $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}$ in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Boundary & Initial Conditions (60s)
lecture_lines: PDE solutions depend on specific boundary constraints.
Initial conditions define the system's state at zero.
Boundary conditions fix behavior at the spatial edges.
animations: Visualize boundary points on the rod in #00FF00.
Show initial temperature distribution curve in #FF0000.
